clue.text: Boxer Muhammad's breaking excellent clinch

indicators.note: the boxer's name breaks into the other word, splitting it open around itself

parts.note: fine means excellent, as in a fine performance
Muhammad Ali was the heavyweight boxer; with the possessive his name gives ALI plus S

explanation.surface: A fight report: Ali's onslaught breaking up a fine clinch in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clinch' looks like boxing vocabulary continuing the scene, but it is the definition in its sense of settle a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To clinch a deal is to settle it conclusively, completing the arrangement.

clue.text: Figure given by Defense Department

definitions.meaning: a geometric figure with five sides
the US Department of Defense is headquartered in, and often named by, its five-sided building in Virginia

explanation.surface: A statistic released by the US military.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-sided shape is a geometric figure, and the US defence headquarters building is named for that shape.

clue.text: Turk, outrageous female removing top

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top, meaning outrageous

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: a woman is a female person

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a Turk and a shocking woman who strips off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing top' takes W off WOMAN, leaving OMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ottoman Empire was the Turkish empire, so an Ottoman is a historic Turk.

clue.text: Lay into cricketer

definitions.meaning: to attack hard with repeated blows, to pound
the player in cricket who wields the bat and faces the bowling

explanation.surface: An instruction to attack a cricket player.
explanation.definitionFit: To pummel someone is to lay into them; the player holding the bat in cricket is likewise named for hitting.

clue.text: Silent when moving? Join commandos, perhaps

indicators.note: the letters of the word silent move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Commando recruits must keep quiet as they move: a training tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing up for military service, for instance with a commando unit, is to join up formally.

clue.text: Now able to use loo in France, you and Latvian showered

parts.note: toi is the French word for you
a Lett is a Latvian
it rained, it showered

explanation.surface: A traveller's mishap: someone used a French loo, then the two of them got soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loo in France' looks like a unit, but 'in France' belongs to 'you', giving the French TOI.
explanation.definitionFit: A child who has learnt to use a lavatory instead of nappies is said to have completed that training.

clue.text: Taking forever, having seconds at dinner?

parts.note: seconds are units of time
at the dinner table one is consuming food

explanation.surface: Someone takes ages over the meal because they keep going back for second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' at dinner suggests second helpings; here it means units of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that takes a long while uses up a great many hours, which is the sense of the compound.

clue.text: When shot, do they lie down? That's confirmed

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the following words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hunter's question: do animals fall over when shot? Settled, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyed-in-the-wool supporter is thoroughly committed, like a confirmed bachelor, set firm in their ways.

clue.text: Sign Schäfer uses confused mutual

indicators.note: confused means jumbled, so the word mutual is mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A German named Schäfer signs a puzzling mutual agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because the clue word Schäfer itself carries the two dots over its a.
explanation.definitionFit: The two dots over the a in a German name like Schäfer are a diacritic mark signalling a vowel change.

clue.text: Blooming apple drink said to be no favourite

parts.note: flowers that are blooming are out

indicators.note: said signals that the drink's name is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: cider is the drink made from apples

explanation.surface: A rustic opinion that flowering-apple cider is nobody's favourite tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns CIDER into a word sounding the same, SIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or competitor not expected to win, the opposite of the favourite, is an unfancied runner.

clue.text: Prepare to shoot for goal

definitions.meaning: to point a gun at a target before firing

explanation.surface: A football coach's instruction: get ready to strike at the net.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointing a weapon at a target before firing, and an objective one strives for, are both senses of the word.

clue.text: On stage in temporary role?

definitions.meaning: performing in a play, as an actor does
standing in for someone, as an interim manager or chairman does

explanation.surface: An understudy performing a part for a short run.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers on stage are doing theatre work; an interim post-holder also carries that title, as in the interim chairman.

clue.text: Where to take off and dry sports kit

parts.note: to air laundry is to dry it
a team's strip is its sports kit

explanation.surface: Changing-room advice on where to undress and hang up your muddy kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' reads as undressing, but it is planes leaving the ground. A strip is British for a team's sports kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing ground is the place aircraft leave the ground from.

clue.text: Tot in poor area beginning to lose out

indicators.note: out means taken away, so a letter is removed from the word for a poor area

parts.note: a slum is a poor area of a town

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A small child in a deprived district starting to miss out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes L, the start of 'lose' from 'beginning to', out of SLUM. 'Tot' looks like a child; it is adding up.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up figures is to add them together, finding a total.

clue.text: Touchy-feely part before news article?

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room
N is short for new, so news, as several new things, is N twice
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A sensitive section placed ahead of a news story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touchy-feely' sounds like emotional openness, but here it literally means used for touching and feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's feeler is the organ it touches and senses with.

clue.text: Egg container overturned

indicators.note: in a down clue overturned means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a tin is a container

explanation.surface: An egg box knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse's egg, found in hair, is a small parasite egg.

clue.text: Gigantic mummy, creature of the night

parts.note: mam is an informal word for mother, like mummy
a moth is a nocturnal insect

explanation.surface: A horror-film billing: a huge Egyptian mummy, monster of the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mummy' suggests an Egyptian corpse; here it is mother, MAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means huge, after the enormous extinct elephant of the ice age.

clue.text: Tree feller an elected council member

parts.note: an alder is a tree
feller is informal for fellow, a man

explanation.surface: A councillor who works as a lumberjack, felling trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree feller' reads as a lumberjack, but 'feller' is a chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior councillor in a borough or city, historically chosen by fellow councillors, holds this title.

clue.text: Tense silence during increased security

indicators.note: during means within, so these pieces sit inside the word for increased

parts.note: more means greater, increased
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
to gag is to silence

explanation.surface: An uneasy hush as security is stepped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'security' suggests guards, but it is the property pledged against a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A home loan is secured on the property, which serves as the lender's security.

clue.text: Bone in neck ape fractured

indicators.note: fractured means broken, so the letters of neck ape are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medical report on a fracture in an ape's neck bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella, the small bone at the front of the knee, is commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Judge initially joining outside court's meeting place

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word
the word for joining goes outside, around, the court abbreviation

parts.note: a union is a joining together
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A judge first marrying a couple outside the courthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting place' suggests a courtroom setting, but it is where roads meet; 'outside' wraps the joining word round the court abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossroads or the point where railway lines meet is a meeting point for routes.

clue.text: Greek sailors dropping with effect of sun's rays

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of, so the abbreviation for with is removed

parts.note: a ship's crew are its sailors
a tan is the browning caused by sunlight

explanation.surface: Sailors on a Greek island flopping in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes W, short for with, out of CREW, leaving CRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete is a Greek island, so a native of it is a Greek.

clue.text: Princess is getting on plane at last

parts.note: someone getting on is growing old

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word plane

explanation.surface: An ageing princess finally boarding her flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting on plane' suggests boarding; 'getting on' means ageing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend and Wagner's opera, the Irish princess loved by Tristan bears this name.

clue.text: Cloud over boat moored in shelter

indicators.note: a vessel moored in a place sits within it, so the boat goes inside

parts.note: a den is a sheltered lair
an ark is a boat, as with Noah

explanation.surface: Skies cloud over a boat tied up in a sheltered harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: When the sky clouds over it grows dim, losing light.

clue.text: Female on farm uses pitcher mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a ewer is a large jug or pitcher

explanation.surface: A farm woman using a water jug for most of her chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the last letter, R, from EWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep, the commonest farmyard female in crosswords.

clue.text: Remote is broken — it's annoying

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters of remote is are reassembled

explanation.surface: The TV remote has stopped working, which is irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wearisome and irksome is irritating and tedious.

clue.text: Right to replace 50 among soldiers in sector

indicators.note: the letter for right is put in place of the Roman fifty

parts.note: a legion is a body of soldiers
L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A military order: switch fifty troops on the right into another sector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' swaps the L of LEGION for R.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is an area or district, and so is a region.

clue.text: Endlessly daring language rattled protective figure

indicators.note: rattled means shaken up, so the letters are jumbled
endlessly means without its end, so the final letter goes

explanation.surface: Bold language that unsettled a bodyguard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts G off 'daring' to give DARIN; 'rattled' shuffles DARIN with LANGUAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit believed to watch over and protect a person is a heavenly guardian.
